newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-UEFA IMPOSE HEAVY FINE ON FERENCVAROS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA IMPOSE HEAVY FINE ON FERENCVAROS.

text.p: Hungarian champions Ferencvaros were fined 100,000 Swiss francs ($80,000) and warned that they could be kicked out of European soccer by UEFA on Friday.
The heavy fine and threatened sanctions were imposed following crowd trouble when Ferencvaros played Olympiakos of Greece in a UEFA Cup, first round, second leg match in Budapest on September 10.

A statement issued after a meeting of UEFA's control and disciplinary committee warned Ferencvaros that their supporters could be banned from their matches, or that the club would be banned from European competition if there was a repeat of the trouble.
Ferencvaros were knocked out of the preliminary round of the European Cup this season by Gothenburg, before switching to the UEFA Cup.
They beat Olympiakos 5-3 on aggregate after winning 3-1 at home and drawing 2-2 away and now face Newcastle United of England in the next round of that competition later this month.

Vitoria Guimaraes of Portugal also received a hefty punishment from UEFA, fined 25,000 Swiss francs ($20,000) because of the bad behaviour of their ball boys during their UEFA Cup first round second leg match against Parma on September 24.
UEFA said the ballboys "behaved in an unsportsmanlike way and willingly delayed the return of the ball on several occasions after it went out of play."
There was also a pitch invasion by photographers and fans threw rolls of paper onto the pitch.
Guimaraes lost the first leg 2-1 but held on to a 2-0 lead for 41 minutes to win the tie 3-2 on aggregate.
